From: Tim Jones <tim.jones@fastgear.com>

Cc: ops@fastgear.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spikes & sharp TPS drop (region us-west-2)

Hi Olga,

Heads up — since ~03:30 UTC our prod traffic to the Redwood hosted API (calls to redwood-moderato-13b-quant) has seen the p95 go from ~300ms to ~1.2s and p99s into the 2.5–3s range. Token-per-second throughput for our steady-state batch has dropped by ~48%. Error rates are climbing (5xx ~1.8%).

This started right after the maintenance window you ran last night — we noticed a change in model variant reported in the client logs (kernel selection: kernel-v1.3.2). Our app traces attached (fastgear_app_trace.log) show long stall times inside the inference call. Can you confirm what was rolled and whether any quantization/profile changes were pushed? This is impacting checkout flows for our biggest customers.

We need an urgent triage and ETA for mitigation. Paging ops@fastgear.com.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Jones
Head of Platform Operations
FastGear

Subject: RE: Production latency spikes & sharp TPS drop (region us-west-2) — triage notes

Quick triage notes from runtime/SRE:

Observations:
- We rolled the quantized kernel selection change (kernel-selector v1.3.2) to hosted us-west-2 at 2026-12-06T22:45:00Z as part of the memory-optimization rollout.
- Telemetry shows increased kernel-selector fallthroughs to the new kv-cache fallback path for the redwood-moderato-13b-quant model. This path has higher per-token overhead in current microcode under high concurrency.
- Repro: We replayed a customer-like traffic shape on a staging pool using v1.3.2 and observed a ~45% reduction in token/s and higher p99s for short-sequence chat workloads.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Pin affected customer requests to kernel-v1.2.* (rollback selector) — fastest to implement (minutes) and low blast radius.
2) Revert quantization profile changes for the model variant — requires model variant rollbacks and re-sync (30–90 min).
3) Increase host burst capacity to absorb latency (short term, costs apply).

Attachments: kernel-selection-diff.txt (diff of selector rules)
Planned next steps:
- I’ll run a controlled pin (1) to a small subset of traffic for FastGear and monitor p95/p99. If it recovers, we’ll expand.
- If pin works, schedule full rollback overnight with product/ops approval.

Vivek
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production latency spikes & sharp TPS drop — quick reproduction and mitigation

Hi all,

I reproduced the regressions in our staging pool with the same model variant and kernel selector. Short summary:

- Baseline (kernel-v1.2.q): 10k tokens/s aggregate, p95 ~0.28s, p99 ~0.45s.
- With kernel-selector v1.3.2 + new quant profile: 5.4k tokens/s, p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~2.7s.

Root cause hypothesis: kernel-selector changes alter the chosen micro-kernel under the quantized path; on current hardware and request size distribution, that path performs worse under sustained concurrency.

Immediate action I executed:
- Pinned FastGear traffic to kernel-v1.2.q on a canary subset (5% traffic) — observed token/s recover to ~9.6k and p95/p99 move back toward baseline within 8 minutes.

Proposal:
- Expand pin to 50% for 30 minutes while we prepare a full rollback for hosted us-west-2.
- Prepare rollback plan and postmortem; attach performance_report.csv and rollback_plan.md.

Tim — do you consent to us widening the pin to 50% now? This will route your traffic to the older selector/kernel for improved throughput.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: performance_report.csv (12KB), rollback_plan.md (4KB)

Mitigation we performed:
- We pinned 5% of your traffic to the previous selector (kernel-v1.2.q) and saw recovery to near-baseline performance in the canary.

Recommended next steps (need your go):
1) Expand the pin to 50% immediately (expected recovery for affected requests within 10 minutes).
2) If recovered, we will schedule a full rollback of kernel-selector v1.3.2 in us-west-2 overnight with a coordinated deployment window (estimated 60–90 minutes).
3) Postmortem and regression tests added to our release gates.

Would you like us to proceed with step (1) now? We can also open a short-call (15 min) with our runtime lead if you prefer.
